reason: The text depicts multiple regular people and communities who consistently demonstrate agency throughout the narrative. Specifically: Zerubbabel and Jeshua (named leaders) actively build the altar; the people gather together as one entity ('וַיֵּאָסְפ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם כְּאִ֥ישׁ אֶחָ֖ד'); priests and Levites perform deliberate religious actions; workers are engaged in construction; the people make offerings to the LORD and celebrate with great shouts; the elderly priests and witnesses weep with emotional agency. Throughout the passage, regular people and communities initiate actions, make decisions, celebrate, and respond—they are not mere passive subjects to divine action but active agents in the rebuilding of the Temple and restoration of worship.
